title: Syntheses at Elevated Temperature and Structures of Lanthanoid/Alkaline Earth Heterobimetallic Derivatives of 2-Methyl-8-hydroxyquinoline

synthesis.procedure: Eu(MQ)3, Mg(MQ)2 and TMB were heated in a sealed, evacuated thick-walled glass tube. In the crystal-isolation preparation, the mixture was held at 270 °C for 18 d, 210 °C for 8 d and 180 °C for 15 d; large red crystals were handpicked from the residual powder. A separate preparation at 210 °C for 21 d also produced the compound, together with Mg4(MQ)8.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Sealed, evacuated thick-walled glass tube; TMB flux
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Flux removed by sublimation under the general procedure; crystals handpicked from residual powder.

source_locations.location: Experimental Section, general procedure and 3[Eu2Mg(MQ)8]·TMB preparations

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The solvate contains three trinuclear Eu–Mg–Eu units per TMB molecule. Each octacoordinate Eu has a terminal chelating MQ ligand and three chelating-bridging MQ ligands; their phenolic oxygen atoms coordinate the hexacoordinate Mg. The crystallographically distinct units include a centrosymmetric, linear unit and noncentrosymmetric, slightly bent units.

synthesis.procedure: Gd(MQ)3, Mg(MQ)2 and TMB were heated in a sealed, evacuated thick-walled glass tube at 210 °C for 21 d. Crystals of the title compound were handpicked from the bulk powder alongside crystals of Mg4(MQ)8.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Flux removed by sublimation under the general procedure; title-compound crystals handpicked from residual powder.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The crystal contains three trinuclear Gd–Mg–Gd units per TMB molecule. Octacoordinate Gd atoms bind terminal chelating and chelating-bridging MQ ligands; bridging phenolic oxygen donors give Mg six-coordinate oxygen environments. Figure 1 depicts a noncentrosymmetric, slightly bent unit.

Each Tb binds one terminal chelating MQ ligand and three MQ ligands that chelate Tb and bridge to Mg through phenolic oxygen; the solvate contains three such units per TMB molecule.

synthesis.procedure: Eu(MQ)3, CaCO3 and TMB were sealed in an evacuated glass tube, heated at 120 °C for 7 d and then at 200 °C for 24 d. Red crystals of [Eu3(MQ)7(CO3)] were handpicked from the bulk powder.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Sealed, evacuated glass tube; TMB flux
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Red crystals handpicked from the bulk powder.

source_locations.location: Structural Studies, carbonate-complex discussion, Figure 5 and Table 6

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Three Eu atoms surround a bridging carbonate in a roughly perpendicular Eu–Eu–Eu arrangement. The two outer Eu atoms are eight-coordinate and each has a terminal MQ chelate and two MQ ligands bridging to the seven-coordinate central Eu. Carbonate chelates both outer Eu atoms and binds the central Eu through one oxygen.

synthesis.procedure: Er(MQ)3, Ca(MQ)2 and TMB were heated in a sealed, evacuated thick-walled glass tube at 270 °C for 18 d, 210 °C for 8 d and 180 °C for 15 d. Red crystals of [Er3(MQ)7(CO3)] were handpicked from the bulk powder. The article attributes the carbonate product to an aged calcium precursor, presumed to have absorbed atmospheric CO2; carbonate formation was not directly established.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Sealed, evacuated thick-walled glass tube; TMB flux
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Flux removed by sublimation under the general procedure; red crystals handpicked from residual powder.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The approximately perpendicular Er–Er–Er arrangement surrounds a μ3-carbonate. Two outer eight-coordinate Er atoms each bind a terminal MQ chelate and two MQ ligands bridging to the central, seven-coordinate Er. Carbonate chelates the outer Er atoms and binds the central Er through an oxygen donor.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The tetranuclear unit adds a third Eu atom above a bent Eu–Ba–Eu arrangement. All four metal atoms are eight-coordinate. Its MQ ligands include terminal chelating, chelating-bridging and ligands bridging three metal centers; two TMB molecules occur as lattice solvate.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: An unsolvated trinuclear Eu–Mg–Eu 8-quinolinolate complex without an inversion center. The Eu–Mg–Eu angle is reported as 176.34(2)°, and the metal–metal distances are effectively equal.
